text: Each REPDF C9 file differs from its original in 12–30 bytes (mean 21.62) at unchanged length; 1,445 of 2,162 changes (66.8%) are inside Flate data, exactly one per damaged stream, across 7–26 damaged streams per file (mean 14.45).
quote: Every file differs in **12–30 bytes (mean 21.62)** at unchanged length. **1,445 of 2,162 changes (66.8%) are inside Flate data, exactly one per damaged stream**, across **7–26 damaged streams per file (mean 14.45)** out of about 34.

text: Only 68 of the C9 byte changes (3.1%) are single-bit, as uniform random replacement predicts (8/255); a bit-flip-only search therefore covers only that share of the damage.
quote: **Only 68 changes (3.1%) are single-bit**, which is exactly what uniform random replacement predicts (8/255)

text: Hamming weights of the C9 byte changes are distributed 1: 68, 2: 253, 3: 509, 4: 582, 5: 456, 6: 220, 7: 66, 8: 8.
The damaged Flate streams in C9 are 854 fonts, 229 text content, 87 graphics content, 175 CMaps, 69 other text and 31 binary streams.
quote: Stream types: 854 fonts, 229 text content, 87 graphics content, 175 CMaps, 69 other text, 31 binary.

text: Byte-fed inflate of the damaged C9 streams: 1,220 of 1,445 (84.4%) decode to the end and fail only Adler-32; 221 (15.3%) raise an inflate error a median of 5 bytes after the damage, and 99.1% of those lie inside the planned [k − 4096, k + 64] window.
quote: **1,220 of 1,445 (84.4%) decode to the end and fail only Adler-32**. **221 (15.3%) raise an inflate error**, a median of **5 bytes** after the damage, and 99.1% of those fall inside the planned [k − 4096, k + 64] window

text: Besides the 1,220 (84.4%) Adler-only and 221 (15.3%) inflate-error streams, 4 damaged C9 streams hit a truncated ('needs more input') end.
quote: Outcomes: **1,220 (84.4%) decode to the end and fail only the Adler-32 check**; 221 (15.3%) raise an inflate error; 4 hit a truncated ("needs more input") end.

text: Inflate-error messages on damaged C9 streams: 'invalid distance too far back' 183, literal/length or code-length set errors 28, 'missing end-of-block' 7, and one each of invalid literal/length code, bad block type and bad zlib header.
quote: Error messages: "invalid distance too far back" 183, literal/length or code-length set errors 28, "missing end-of-block" 7, invalid literal/length code 1, bad block type 1, bad zlib header 1.

text: For inflate-error C9 streams the distance from damage to error is p10 1, p25 3, median 5, p75 16, p90 68, p95 675, p99 3,025, max 6,623 bytes.
quote: Quantiles of (error offset k − true offset): p10 = 1, p25 = 3, median 5, p75 16, p90 68, p95 675, p99 3,025, max 6,623 bytes.

text: In 1,500 synthetic random byte replacements, inflate errors fired 44.5% of the time when the damage was in the first 4 KiB of output, 10.9% in 4–32 KiB and 0.5% beyond 32 KiB.
quote: Across 1,500 random replacements, inflate errors fired **44.5% of the time in the first 4 KiB of output, 10.9% in 4–32 KiB, and 0.5% beyond 32 KiB**.

text: Synthetic single-byte replacements: 80.9% Adler-only, 18.3% inflate error, 0.7% truncated end, 0.1% no effect.
quote: Outcomes: 80.9% Adler-only, 18.3% inflate error, 0.7% truncated end, 0.1% no effect.

text: In the synthetic replication the early-error rate is 7.3% for fonts, 29.7% for content streams and 41.8% for CMaps.
quote: Early-error rate by type: fonts 7.3%, content 29.7%, CMaps 41.8%.

text: A DEFLATE block census finds exactly one stored block in 3,398 original streams; 94% of text content streams and 100% of CMaps are a single dynamic block, so stored-block resync almost never applies.
quote: finds **exactly one stored block in 3,398 streams**. **94% of text content streams and 100% of CMaps are a single dynamic block.**

text: 31.6% of Adler-only damaged streams keep the original decoded length; for those the median number of wrong bytes is 5 (p10 = 1, p75 = 18, p90 = 70) and the median fraction correct is 99.99%.
quote: 31.6% keep the original decoded length. For those, the median number of wrong bytes is 5 (p10 = 1, p75 = 18, p90 = 70) and the median fraction of correct bytes is 99.99%.

text: Mean correct prefix over all damaged streams is 48.1% of decoded bytes, and prefix plus common suffix gives 59.0%; for Adler-only streams the figures are 53.6% and 66.6%.
quote: Across all damaged streams, the mean correct prefix is 48.1% of the decoded bytes; prefix plus common suffix gives 59.0% (Adler-only streams: 53.6% → 66.6%).

text: With miniz_oxide, a cloned DecompressorOxide checkpoint is 10,504 bytes and the streaming InflateState is 43,296 bytes.
quote: a checkpoint is 10,504 bytes; the streaming `InflateState` is 43,296 bytes.

text: On the inflate-error C9 streams, a checkpointed all-byte-values search scanning backward from the error offset fixed 218 of 221 (98.6%), all byte-exact, median 13.5 ms and p90 129 ms per stream.
quote: the search **fixed 218 of 221 (98.6%), all byte-exact, with a median of 13.5 ms and p90 of 129 ms**

text: The inflate-error search tried 8.2 M candidates in 229 s in total, about 28 µs per candidate.
quote: 8.2 M candidates took 229 s in total, about 28 µs per candidate.

text: On Adler-only C9 streams of 4 KiB or less, a full-range all-byte-values search accepted 245 of 245 (243 byte-exact), median 0.23 s.
quote: On Adler-only streams of 4 KiB or less, a full-range search accepted **245 of 245 (243 exact), median 0.23 s**.

text: For the sampled mid-size Adler-only streams, an unlocalized full-range search fixed 158 of 239 (66%), all exact, and 81 timed out.
quote: **158/239 (66%) fixed, all exact; 81 timed out.**

text: A grammar localizer flags the first ungrammatical content or CMap token in 85% of Adler-only text streams, and the true damage lies within [flag − 64, flag + 8] in 91.8% of flagged streams.
quote: localizer flags the first ungrammatical content or CMap token in **85%** of Adler-only text streams. The true damage lies within [flag − 64, flag + 8] in 91.8% of those.

text: Of the Adler-only content, CMap and other-text streams, 343 (85%) contain a grammar violation and 60 (15%) look grammatical.
quote: The originals all pass the tokenizer. In the damaged versions, 343 (85%) contain a grammar violation and 60 (15%) look grammatical.

text: The true damaged offset lies within [flag − 64, flag + 8] in 91.8% of grammar-flagged streams, within 256 in 94.8%, within 1,024 in 95.9% and within 4,096 in 98.8%.
quote: The true offset lies within [flag − 64, flag + 8] in 91.8% of flagged cases, within 256 in 94.8%, within 1,024 in 95.9%, and within 4,096 in 98.8%.

text: Searching [flag − 256, flag + 8] around the grammar flag fixed 324 of 343 flagged streams (94.5%), median 25 ms.
quote: Searching [flag − 256, flag + 8] fixed **324 of 343 flagged streams (94.5%), median 25 ms**.

text: In the grammar-localized search three streams timed out and in 16 the damage lay outside the window.
quote: Three timeouts; in 16 cases the damage lay outside the window.

text: Fonts are 798 of the 1,220 Adler-only C9 streams (median 16.2 KiB compressed), and an unlocalized search finished only 66% of 4–16 KiB streams within 20 s.
quote: They are **798 of the 1,220 Adler-only streams**, with a median of 16.2 KiB compressed. An unlocalized search finished only **66% of 4–16 KiB streams within 20 s**.

text: All 12,532 tables in the 854 intact embedded fonts have valid checksums, and the first table whose checksum fails contains the damage in 765 of 766 damaged fonts, averaging 36.9% of the font (claim only: no committed script, E6).
quote: All 12,532 tables in the 854 intact fonts had valid checksums. The first table whose checksum fails contains the damage in **765 of 766** damaged fonts, and it averages 36.9% of the font

text: PR16 committed no script for the TrueType localizer (E6), and its search cost was not measured.
quote: No script for this localizer (E6) is committed, and its search cost is unmeasured.

text: Adler-32 false accepts occurred: one accept among 245 small streams was a genuine collision on 2.7 KB of output, and another came from damage to the Adler trailer itself.
quote: One accept in 245 small streams was a genuine collision on 2.7 KB of output. Another came from damage to the Adler trailer itself.

text: Measured Adler false accepts were 1/245 (full-range small streams) and 1/324 (grammar-localized), against the design's 'Adler-32 or valid content' acceptance.
quote: | Acceptance | Adler-32 *or* "valid content" | Adler false accepts: 1/245 and 1/324 |

text: The proposed changes make about 39% of all damaged C9 streams byte-exact on demonstrated numbers, against at most 3% under the current plan; a font localizer plausibly takes this to 60–70% (an estimate).
quote: Together these changes make **about 39% of all damaged streams byte-exact on demonstrated numbers**, compared with at most 3% under the current plan. Adding the font localizer plausibly takes this to 60–70%.

text: The 39% total is (218 + 324 + ~20 small fonts) out of 1,445 damaged Flate streams.
quote: Est. total: ≈39% of all damaged Flate streams byte-exact demonstrated (218 + 324 + ~20 small fonts out of 1,445)

text: The font-localizer projection is an estimate; all gains are counted in stream bytes and their effect on REPDF's OCR word metric was not measured.
quote: That figure is an estimate, not a measurement. All gains are counted in stream bytes. Their effect on REPDF's OCR word metric was not measured.

text: Every C10 file is cut at exactly 70.0%; in Print to PDF files 35.6% of text content-stream bytes and 45.7% of DCT image bytes lie after the cut, giving a content-byte ceiling of about 64% versus REPDF's 35.35%.
quote: Every C10 file is cut at exactly **70.0%**. In "Save As" files, all content streams and images lie before the cut. In "Print to PDF" files, **35.6% of text content-stream bytes and 45.7% of DCT image bytes lie after it**. That sets a ceiling of about 64% by content bytes, well above REPDF's 35.35%.

text: 92 of the 97 streams that straddle the C10 cut are fonts (E8 census, no committed script).
quote: **92 of the 97 streams that straddle the cut are fonts** (E8 census; no script committed).

text: REPDF's own tables disagree: C10 Print to PDF is 35.35% in Table 2 but 30.49% in Table 5, and C9 is 60.11% in Table 2 but 58.77/62.70 in Table 5.
quote: Table 2's per-language means give C10 "Print to PDF" **35.35%**, the figure the text quotes in §5.4. Table 5's tool comparison gives **30.49%**. C9 is 60.11% in Table 2 but 58.77/62.70 in Table 5.

text: All 50 Save As originals use xref streams and object streams, yet all 300 page dictionaries and every Font/FontDescriptor dictionary are top-level objects; all 50 Print to PDF originals use classic xref tables (ad hoc corpus scan, no committed script).
quote: **All 50 "Save As" originals use xref streams and object streams, but all 300 page dictionaries and every Font/FontDescriptor dictionary sit at top level.** **All 50 "Print to PDF" originals use classic xref tables**

text: The Save As originals use 44 distinct /BaseFont names, most commonly Cambria (45 files), Rubik-Medium (37), Bricolage Grotesque Light (35), Oswald-Medium (34), NotoSerif-Thin (34) and Poppins-Bold (32) (ad hoc corpus scan, no committed script).
quote: The same corpus scan counted **44 distinct `/BaseFont` names** in the "Save As" originals. The most common are Cambria (45 files), Rubik-Medium (37), Bricolage Grotesque Light (35), Oswald-Medium (34), NotoSerif-Thin (34) and Poppins-Bold (32)

text: Only two of the Save As BaseFont faces are Noto faces, and Print to PDF files carry only anonymous CIDFont+Fn names, so a Noto-only glyph-map database cannot decode the corpus.
quote: **Only two are Noto faces.** "Print to PDF" files carry only `CIDFont+F1`–`F22`

text: Across four fonts, pairs disagree in advance width on 51–72 of 73 common characters, and widths cut English letter uncertainty from 4.18 bits to 2.10 (Arial-metric) and 1.88 (Times-metric), and to 0.28–0.57 bits for fonts with more varied widths.
quote: font pairs disagree on **51–72 of 73 common characters**, so a dozen used codes fingerprint a font and its gid space. Widths also cut English letter uncertainty from **4.18 bits to 2.10** (Arial-metric) and **1.88** (Times-metric), and to 0.28–0.57 bits for fonts with more varied widths.

text: Widths carry no information for Han: all 20,940 WenQuanYi Han glyphs are 1000 units wide.
quote: They carry **no information for Han**: all 20,940 WenQuanYi Han glyphs are 1000 units wide.

text: lopdf recovers a stream length only when exactly one EOL-framed 'endstream endobj' exists within the object's bounds.
quote: lopdf recovers a stream length only when **exactly one** EOL-framed `endstream endobj` exists within the object's bounds

text: lopdf accepts object headers only at the start of a line, because strings and comments in non-stream objects can contain convincing 'N G obj' text.
quote: It also accepts object headers only at the start of a line. That second rule exists because literal strings and comments inside *non-stream* objects can contain convincing `12 0 obj` text.

text: qpdf rejects a recovered stream length that would swallow another object's header.
quote: qpdf adds a cross-check: it rejects a recovered length that would swallow another object's header

text: MuPDF refuses to let a truncated object at EOF overwrite a good copy during repair.
quote: MuPDF refuses to let "a truncated object at EOF overwrite a good one"

text: pdf.js lets a later duplicate object copy win only if it parses.
quote: pdf.js lets a later copy win only if it parses

text: Under 'last in byte order wins' a truncated incremental update would shadow complete earlier revisions; the rule should be last well-formed copy wins, with each generation a distinct key.
quote:
Under the design's "last in byte order wins", a truncated incremental update would shadow complete earlier revisions. That is exactly the C10 case.

The rule should be **last *well-formed* copy wins, with each generation a distinct key**.

text: MuPDF's bug-708286 rule gives an object-stream member its container's byte offset, so a later uncompressed copy beats it.
quote: adopt MuPDF's bug-708286 rule: a compressed member takes its container's byte offset, so a later uncompressed copy beats it

text: pdf.js and hayro validate Root candidates: Root must lead to a Pages dict, which must lead to a Kids array or an integer Count.
quote: Root selection should validate candidates the way pdf.js and hayro do: Root must lead to a Pages dict, which must lead to a Kids array or integer Count

text: lopdf 0.45 corrects startxref and /Prev offsets within ±64 bytes.
quote: Declared offsets are noisy evidence, not garbage. lopdf 0.45 corrects `startxref` and `/Prev` within ±64 bytes

text: qpdf rebases every offset on a %PDF header found anywhere in the first 1 KiB, fixing the junk-prefix case.
quote: qpdf rebases every offset on a header found anywhere in the first 1 KiB, which fixes the junk-prefix case behind half of Jones's bad xrefs

text: qpdf and hayro accept a bare CR after 'stream', which the design's §20 rejects; before 'endstream' exactly one EOL should be stripped.
quote: §20 rejects a bare CR after `stream`, but qpdf accepts it because "some readers, including Adobe reader, accept a carriage return by itself", and hayro accepts it too

text: qpdf's page-tree recovery climbs /Parent, drops duplicate pages and pages with more than two errors, keeps visited sets over /Kids arrays and caps depth at 100.
quote: It drops a page that appears twice in recovery mode, and a page with more than two errors. It keeps visited sets over `/Kids` arrays as well as nodes. And it caps depth at 100.

text: qpdf 12.2 ignores recovered arrays and dictionaries with more than 5,000 elements.
quote: qpdf 12.2 now ignores recovered arrays and dicts with more than 5,000 elements

text: Shadow attacks on signed PDFs fooled 16 of 29 viewers, so shadowed revisions are forensic evidence.
quote: turns "last wins" into forensic evidence. Shadow attacks fooled **16 of 29 viewers**

text: No surveyed engine uses decompression to find a stream's extent; all fall back to the first endstream, and Poppler overrides a correct /Length in reconstructed mode.
quote: **No engine uses decompression to find a stream's extent.** All fall back to the first `endstream`, and Poppler even overrides a correct `/Length` in reconstructed mode

text: MuPDF, PDFium, pdf.js, qpdf and pypdf harvest the trailer dictionary of xref streams (Root, Info, ID, Encrypt, Size), which the design discards as diagnosis only.
quote: That discards the trailer dictionary MuPDF, PDFium, pdf.js, qpdf and pypdf all harvest (Root, Info, ID, Encrypt, Size).

text: Because both toolpaths run in seconds, selection should be generate-and-validate rather than predict-then-act.
quote: The algorithm-selection literature therefore points to **generate-and-validate**, not predict-then-act.

text: In automated program repair, 104 of 110 plausible GenProg patches amounted to deleting functionality (Qi et al., as cited).
quote: **104 of 110 "plausible" GenProg patches amounted to deleting functionality**

text: PR16 proposes a plausible-but-wrong rate: the share of outputs that pass every gate yet fall below the target recovery.
quote: Report a **plausible-but-wrong rate**, the share of outputs that pass every gate yet fall below the target recovery.

text: Confidence should be calibrated with Platt scaling because the calibration set will have fewer than about 1,000 slots.
quote: Calibrate it with Platt scaling, since the calibration set will have fewer than about 1,000 slots

text: Certifying at most 2% wrong auto-picks at 95% confidence needs roughly 150 error-free labelled slots (rule of three), replacing the 0.35 threshold with a risk-targeted one.
quote: Choose the auto-accept threshold from a target selective risk with a finite-sample bound, in place of the magic 0.35 ([Geifman & El-Yaniv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.08500)). Certifying at most 2% wrong auto-picks at 95% confidence needs roughly 150 error-free labelled slots, by the rule of three.

text: PDFPundit's planned Dice metric over a Myers alignment equals LCS-F1 and is not comparable with REPDF's OCR word recall on renders.
quote: **PDFPundit's planned metric is not comparable with REPDF's.** Dice over a Myers alignment, `2·matched/(len_orig + len_repaired)`, is exactly LCS-F1.

text: In a study of 11 readers the best render comparators (CW-SSIM, pHash) still paid a 50% false-positive rate for an 80% true-positive rate (Kuchta et al., as cited).
quote: In a study of 11 readers, CW-SSIM and pHash were the best render comparators, and even so **an 80% true-positive rate cost a 50% false-positive rate**

text: Splits must group by base document; a 60/20/20 grouped split leaves only about 10 documents in the sealed test.
quote: A 60/20/20 grouped split leaves only about 10 documents in the sealed test.

text: Since REPDF publishes only aggregates, the defensible claim is non-inferiority: PDFPundit's lower 95% bound on REPDF's metric, per stratum, is at least REPDF's point estimate minus a stated margin.
quote: It holds when the lower 95% bound of PDFPundit's result, using REPDF's metric in the same stratum, is at least REPDF's point estimate minus a stated margin.

text: A held-out corruptor family (multi-byte bursts, variable truncation, shifted xrefs, partial /Kids damage) should be run only at release as the overfitting indicator.
quote: Finally, run a **held-out corruptor family** only at release: multi-byte bursts, variable truncation, shifted rather than deleted xrefs, and partial `/Kids` damage.

text: PR16's E6 and E8 have no committed scripts, the builder of mzbench's cases directory was not saved, and mzbench ran on miniz_oxide 0.8.9 while the design pins 0.9.
quote: First, E6 (the TrueType localizer) and E8 (the C10 census) have no committed scripts. Second, the step that built mzbench's per-stream `cases/` directory was not saved ([experiments README](../experiments/README.md)). Third, `mzbench` ran on `miniz_oxide` 0.8.9 while the design pins 0.9

text: The font-name and ObjStm scan of the corpus was run ad hoc and is uncommitted.
quote: The font-name and ObjStm scan of the corpus quoted in this report was run ad hoc during synthesis and is also uncommitted.

text: Ranked design change: rebuild the C9 ladder with keep-all ChecksumMismatch, a checkpointed 255-value search, err-offset/grammar/TrueType/small-stream localizers, Adler-required acceptance, Brown resync, and a C9 fixture of one random byte per stream plus non-Flate hits.
quote: Rebuild the C9 ladder: `ChecksumMismatch` keep-all; checkpointed 255-value search; err-offset, grammar, TrueType and small-stream localizers; Adler-required acceptance with tie-breaks; Brown resync replacing stored blocks; C9 fixture = one random byte per stream across many streams, plus non-Flate hits

text: Ranked design change: decode through the document's own fonts (the ISO §9.10.2 ladder first, glyph maps for the corpus faces and system fonts, width fingerprinting, decipherment) and drop inference only from the bundled DB.
quote: Decode through the document's fonts: §9.10.2 ladder first; glyph maps for the corpus's Google/Office faces and for installed system fonts; width fingerprinting; decipherment back-end; drop "inference only from bundled DB"

text: Ranked design change: treat C6 as orphan font re-linking per (page, slot) and ignore CIDFont+Fn names.
quote: C6 as orphan re-linking per (page, slot); ignore `CIDFont+Fn` names

text: Ranked design change: gid-to-String maps, word-level shaping, BTreeMap<u16,String> ToUnicode and /ActualText spans for Arabic and Devanagari.
quote: `gid → String` maps, word-level shaping, `BTreeMap<u16,String>` ToUnicode, `/ActualText` spans

text: Ranked design change: well-formed-last-wins with a truncation guard, per-generation keys, ObjStm container-offset precedence, phantom-header guards, unique-endstream rule, probe-end guard, bare CR, strip one EOL, caps, /Size = max+1 and determinism.
quote: Well-formed-last-wins with truncation guard; per-gen keys; ObjStm container-offset precedence; line-start/non-stream phantom guard; unique-`endstream` rule; probe-end guard; accept bare CR; strip one EOL; caps; `/Size` = max+1; determinism

text: Ranked design change: xref-stream dictionaries as trailer candidates, validated Root, ±64 B and header-relative offsets, page-tree dedupe, cycle sets, depth cap and orphan-page scoring.
quote: Xref-stream dicts as trailer candidates; validated Root; ±64 B and header-relative offsets; page-tree dedupe, cycle sets, depth cap, orphan-page scoring

text: Ranked design change: generate-and-validate with retention, blank-page and agreement gates, dropping the 0.60 constant and adding a plausible-but-wrong KPI.
quote: Generate-and-validate with retention/blank/agreement gates; drop the 0.60 constant; plausible-but-wrong KPI

text: Ranked design change: a length-aware calibrated posterior, a risk-targeted threshold, escalation reasons and a 'type what you see' prompt.
quote: Length-aware calibrated posterior; risk-targeted threshold; escalation reasons; "type what you see" prompt

text: Ranked design change: REPDF-comparable OCR recall in the harness, decomposed text metrics, grouped splits, held-out corruptors, an external oracle battery and a per-file PR gate.
quote: REPDF-comparable OCR recall in the harness; decomposed text metrics; grouped splits; held-out corruptors; external oracle battery; per-file PR gate

text: Ranked design change: salvage truncated font tables and glyphs, decode JPEG/JPX leniently and route truncated Flate to Prefix for C10.
quote: Truncated-font table/glyph salvage; lenient JPEG/JPX decode; route truncated Flate to `Prefix`

text: Ranked design change: add ObjStm/xref-stream, incremental-chain, linearized, CR/LF, sector-hole and multi-fault damage classes, Common Crawl truncation pairs, the Stressful corpus and revision-history Findings.
quote: Add ObjStm/xref-stream, incremental-chain, linearized, CR/LF, sector-hole and multi-fault classes; CC truncation pairs; Stressful corpus; revision-history and signature-shadow Findings
